text:
lee: Heads up: noticed a cluster of support tickets where tenants were surprised by billing after using X-Api-Version on /v1 paths. We should decide how this affects our deprecation messaging and console UX.

anu: Can you share the example?

lee: Example repro (minimal):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n  -H 'X-Api-Version: 2' \n  -d '{"model":"embed-small","inputs":["a","b"]}'
```

lee: Router falls back to v2 handler; both router and handler currently emit usage events so tenants see inflated counts.

marco: This surfaced during the v1->v2 compatibility rollout. We had a few choices before: change routing semantics (only final handler emits), or keep semantics and adjust billing pipeline to dedupe. Which do we prefer?

anu: My vote: change routing semantics so only one billing emitter is allowed per request. Simpler for tenants and aligns with intuitive expectation. But we must be careful about streaming vs batch differences.

marco: Agreed on semantics, but implementation touches a lot of proxies. Short-term alternative: router emits a signed internal header X-Redwood-Metered-Signed when it emits, backend verifies signature before emitting. That prevents spoofing but requires key rotation plumbing.

lee: Key rotation is heavier. For hotfix we can strip inbound X-Redwood-Metered* headers at edge, and add a boolean X-Redwood-Metered set by router for internal hops only (strip at edge). Backend checks for presence and suppresses duplicate meter. That’s quick and low risk.

anu: UX side: update deprecation docs to say "Header-based version negotiation may cause compatibility fallthrough and affect usage metrics. Prefer explicit /v2/ paths when setting X-Api-Version:2." Add a prominent console banner for tenants who hit mixed-version calls in the last 7 days.

marco: Also product asks for a per-tenant "compatibility mode" toggle in the Console: if enabled, router will auto-route header-negotiated calls to v2 variants without emitting route-level billing. That gives customers control.

product-bot: Feature request created: PROD-4410 (compat mode toggle).

ops-bot: Canary scheduled: router-meter-suppress -> 4% at 1744312000. Smoke: compare raw_meter vs deduped_meter delta < 0.2%

anu: Telemetry: add metric negotiated_fallbacks and negotiated_billed_mismatch to help validate. Alert if mismatch_rate > 0.25% in a 5m window.

lee: For billing: billing team wants to compute delta and backfill credits for tenants that crossed quota due to this. We have 5d of raw logs, should be enough.

marco: One more policy decision: should we classify these as "implementation noise" or as a "breaking behavior" for deprecation timeline? If it’s noise we fix quietly. If it’s breaking we need a longer comms window.

anu: It's noise from our routing internals. Fix + short notice is fine. We should still post a brief console note explaining what happened and how credits are handled.

lee: OK owners: marco -> router patch + header-strip, anu -> docs + console banner + telemetry, lee -> billing delta/credits contact. Marco please ensure header is only honored internally and edge strips any client-supplied header.

marco: Will do. PR target today. I'll coordinate canary and smoke signals with ops-bot.

product-bot: PROD-4411 created: billing credit flow doc.

lee: After canary, short postmortem and a small UI annotation in billing timeline. Keep comms concise. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
